les: Hoe ver is dit regtig van hier na daar
kaps_punt: Skale: Meet reguitlyn-afstande tussen stede op 'n Suid-Afrikaanse en die wêreldkaart

items.bewering: Die pad uit jou dorp draai om koppies en volg die rivier.
items.blok: Die pad draai en die reguit lyn nie
items.bron: Ordnance Survey Mapzone, 'Measuring Distance' (2015), ordnancesurvey.co.uk/mapzone/assets/doc/map-skills/Measuring-Distance-en.pdf: 'If you're following a road or footpath, it can change direction many times to avoid things like woods and rivers.' The sentence is an illustrative scenario, not a claim about every town.

items.bewering: 'n Voël hoef nie een van daardie draaie te maak nie. Hy kan reguit van die een dorp tot by die ander vlieg. Die afstand langs daardie reguit lyn is die reguitlyn-afstand tussen die twee plekke.
items.blok: Die pad draai en die reguit lyn nie
items.bron: Ordnance Survey Mapzone 'Measuring Distance': 'Measuring in straight lines is sometimes called as the crow flies ... to find out how far one town or city is from another'; writingexplained.org idiom entry (straight-line distance ignoring roads and terrain). Mapping checked: the bird stands for the idealised straight path, which is the established English idiom; the lesson says the bird CAN fly straight, not that birds always do, so a learner reasoning on from it reaches the right idea (distance ignoring obstacles) and nothing false.

items.bewering: Elke draai in 'n pad sit nog 'n stukkie by die reis. Die pad is daarom nooit korter as die reguit lyn nie.
items.blok: Die pad draai en die reguit lyn nie
items.bron: Implicit superlative (the straight line is the shortest). Ordnance Survey Mapzone 'Measuring Distance' (travel routes are longer than the straight line because they change direction); writingexplained.org: road distance is usually longer than the as-the-crow-flies distance. Holds on the earth's surface as well: the great-circle line is the shortest surface path, and a road on the surface can at best equal it (airmilescalculator.com/distance/cpt-to-lhr: flown route about 1.7% longer than great-circle). 'nooit korter' is the right strength; 'nie langer nie' would have been false and it does not say that.

items.bewering: Kies twee stede op 'n kaart van Suid-Afrika en merk elkeen met 'n potlood. Hou die 0 van jou lineaal by die een punt en lê die rand teen die ander punt. Lees by daardie ander punt af hoeveel sentimeter dit is.
items.blok: Merk twee stede en meet met 'n lineaal
items.bron: osmaps.com/discover/guides/beginners-guide-to-measuring-distance-on-a-map (Ordnance Survey): measure in centimetres with a ruler, then convert with the map's scale. The instruction correctly says to put the 0 mark (not the end of the ruler) on the first point, which avoids the common error where a ruler's 0 is set in from its edge.

items.bewering: Daardie sentimeters sê nog niks oor die werklike afstand op die aarde nie.
items.bron: Ordnance Survey Mapzone 'Measuring Distance': the scale 'converts the distance you measure on a map (usually in centimetres or inches) into a real life distance'. Without a scale the map measurement gives no ground distance.

items.bewering: As jou kaart 'n woordskaal het en nie groter of kleiner gekopieer is nie, sê die woordskaal hoeveel kilometer een sentimeter voorstel.
items.bron: Esri ArcGIS Blog on verbal scales (esri.com/arcgis-blog/?p=120441, via search extract): verbal scales, like representative fractions, become invalid if the map is enlarged or reduced; Massey University GIS 'Guide to map scale' (gisweb.massey.ac.nz): a bar scale in a photocopy gives the new scale. The condition is correct and is the right one to attach to this route. Note for the human, not a fault: the condition names copying; a map shown zoomed on a screen breaks a word scale in exactly the same way, and the lesson does not say so. It is not false as written.

items.bewering: Neem as voorbeeld 'n woordskaal waar een sentimeter 250 kilometer voorstel. As jy dan vyf sentimeter meet, maal jy vyf met 250 en kry omtrent 1 250 kilometer.
items.bron: Arithmetic: 5 x 250 = 1 250. Correct, and multiplying the measured centimetres by the kilometres per centimetre is the correct operation (osmaps.com guide: measure in cm, multiply by the scale). 'omtrent' is appropriate for a ruler reading. The 1 cm : 250 km scale is a plausible small atlas scale for South Africa (country about 1 600 km wide, so about 6.4 cm on the page).

items.bewering: 'n Papiertjie se reguit rand het geen merke nie en kan jou dus geen sentimeter gee nie. Daarom werk hierdie roete net op 'n kaart met 'n lynskaal.
items.blok: Die tweede roete: 'n papiertjie en die lynskaal
items.bron: Exclusivity claim ('net'). National Geographic Education, 'Measuring distances on a map' (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/measuring-distances-on-a-map): the paper strip is read against the map's scale bar; Ordnance Survey Mapzone: paper edge placed 'against the scale bar'. Tested as a set with the ruler route: ruler needs a word scale and an unresized map; paper needs a line scale and is unaffected by resizing (Esri/Massey above). Each condition is stated correctly and neither route is claimed to work where it does not. A map carrying only a ratio scale (1:10 000 000) is served by neither route as described; that is an omission, not a false statement.

items.bewering: Lê die rand teen die twee stede en trek 'n strepie by elkeen. Hou dan die eerste strepie by die 0 van die lynskaal. Waar die tweede strepie val, lees jy die kilometers af.
items.blok: Die tweede roete: 'n papiertjie en die lynskaal
items.bron: Ordnance Survey / map-skills guidance via search extract: 'Place a straight edge of paper on the map, so it touches both points ... Make sure the first point you marked is on zero. Wherever the second point is on the scale bar, that is your straight-line distance.' The lesson's steps match in order and substance, and give a straight-line distance (the right kind).

items.bewering: Is die afstand langer as die lynskaal, skuif die papiertjie aan en tel die stukke bymekaar.
items.blok: Die tweede roete: 'n papiertjie en die lynskaal
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Measuring distances on a map': extend the scale by adding segments to the paper; Nebraska Department of Education 'Measuring Nebraska' lesson (education.ne.gov): mark at the scale's maximum, slide that mark back to 0, repeat, and total the lengths. Same method.

items.bewering: Doen nou dieselfde met Kaapstad en Londen op 'n kaart van die wêreld. Jou antwoord is hier net 'n skatting.
items.blok: Nou op die kaart van die wêreld
items.bron: True great-circle distance Cape Town-London Heathrow about 9 680 km (airmilescalculator.com/distance/cpt-to-lhr; 1flt.com 9 681 km). Checked what a learner following either route would get: on a Mercator world map with an equator scale bar (scale grows with sec of latitude, USGS Professional Paper 1395 plate 1; bluemarblegeo Mercator page) the straight line measures about 10 900 km, roughly 13% too long (my calculation from the Mercator formula: north-south 1.68 rad, east-west 18.5 degrees); on a plain latitude-longitude world map about 9 700 km. So the answer depends on the map and is an estimate, exactly as the lesson says; the method still yields a straight-line distance of the right kind.

items.bewering: Die aarde is 'n bal en 'n blad papier is nie. 'n Plat kaart van die hele wêreld rek party dele van die aarde uit of druk hulle saam.
items.blok: Nou op die kaart van die wêreld
items.bron: USGS 'Map Projections' poster and Circular 982 (pubs.usgs.gov/circ/1986/0982): every flat map misrepresents the earth's surface; a map can preserve some but never all of true distances, directions, areas, shapes; on the Mercator distances are grossly distorted near the poles. Mapping checked: 'bal' for a near-spherical earth is sound at Grade 6, and 'rek uit of druk saam' correctly describes scale varying across the map; a learner reasoning on reaches 'distances on a world map are unreliable in places', which is true.

items.bewering: Op 'n kaart van net Suid-Afrika is daardie rek of saamdruk so klein dat die antwoord bruikbaar bly.
items.blok: Nou op die kaart van die wêreld
items.bron: USGS (Circular 982 / projections poster): distortion largely disappears when a properly chosen projection covers a small area. OSGeo Africa list, July 2016 (lists.osgeo.org/pipermail/africa/2016-July/002775.html), South African government GIS practitioner: the NGI 1:2 200 000 National Map of South Africa uses Albers equal-area conic, standard parallels about 24 and 33 S chosen to minimise distortion over 22-35 S; a comparable Albers layout over the wider USA has about 1.25% maximum scale error (Bentley reference). Worst plausible case a learner might own, a web-Mercator map of South Africa, varies by about plus or minus 7% around mid-country (sec 22 = 1.08, sec 35 = 1.22). 'bruikbaar' with 'omtrent' holds in both cases.

items.bewering: Jy kan van twee plekke op 'n kaart van Suid-Afrika sê omtrent hoe ver hulle van mekaar is. Jy hoef dit in geen boek of op geen foon te gaan naslaan nie.
items.blok: Wat jy nou self kan uitwerk
items.bron: Follows from the two routes verified above (Ordnance Survey; National Geographic Education) and the small distortion on a South African map (USGS; OSGeo Africa/NGI). 'omtrent' is the right strength.

items.bewering: Op 'n wêreldkaart is die antwoord vir plekke soos Kaapstad en Londen 'n growwe skatting.
items.blok: Wat jy nou self kan uitwerk
items.bron: Same evidence as the Cape Town-London item above: measured results range from about 0.5% to about 13% off the 9 680 km great-circle distance depending on the world map's projection. 'growwe skatting' is accurate.

items.bewering: Vir plekke ver noord, ver suid of aan teenoorgestelde kante van die kaart kan dit heeltemal verkeerd wees.
items.blok: Wat jy nou self kan uitwerk
items.bron: USGS: on a world Mercator, distances are grossly distorted near the polar regions and scale becomes infinite at the poles. Britannica 'Bering Strait' (britannica.com/place/Bering-Strait): Asia and North America about 85 km apart at the strait, yet on an Atlantic-centred world map Chukotka and Alaska sit at opposite edges, so a straight line across the map would be wrong by most of the earth's circumference. 'kan ... heeltemal verkeerd wees' is correct and correctly hedged with 'kan'.

items.bewering: reguitlyn-afstand: Die reguit afstand tussen twee plekke, en nie die padafstand nie.
items.bron: Read alone, with the rest of the lesson deleted: it is circular in wording (reguit afstand) but true, and the contrast with road distance is the standard one (Ordnance Survey Mapzone 'Measuring Distance', 'as the crow flies'; writingexplained.org). Nothing in it a learner could take as false. Over intercontinental distances a literal 'straight' line would pass through the earth, but in map work the term conventionally means the shortest distance over the surface, and the entry does not claim otherwise.

opsomming: All seventeen claims check out, including the 5 x 250 = 1 250 km example, both measuring methods and the conditions each needs, and the accuracy claims (usable on a South African map, a rough estimate for Cape Town to London, possibly completely wrong far north or south or across the map's edges); the only gap a person might want to look at is that the word-scale condition mentions copying but not a map zoomed on a screen, which is incomplete rather than false.
